author: potuz
content: Hey, I've hit this problem on implementation now, not sure who to ask from vouch, perhaps <@737740104281489531> knows? the issue is what should the endpoint return for `execution_payload_value` when a beacon block is requested. I assume multi-CLs like Vouch would want to get the block that will pay the most, but how do we deal with bids that include trusted payments? are these added to the `execution_payload_value` or not?

author: potuz
content: What are clients doing for this?

author: serenita_io
content:
Related discussion here - https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/631#discussion_r3655399777 .
In my opinion it technically should include it - `execution_payload_value = bid.value + bid.execution_payment` (careful, one is in Gwei and the other in Wei).
If a client doesn't allow/support trusted bids, the calculation still works the same way, the `bid.execution_payment` part will just be zero, right?

author: potuz
content: Yeah this makes sense to me, afaik the only consumer of this value is someone that will be comparing blocks to choose one right? So it's either these or include both the trusted and trustless value separated. So are all clients including the sum here?

author: nflaig
content: the spec says `total value of the bid`, so yes, clients should return the sum, ie. `execution_payload_value = bid.value + bid.execution_payment` as Luca pointed out

author: nflaig
content: but I expect both Vero and Vouch to implement BYOB, so it will not be relevant for them I suppose

author: serenita_io
content: There is the possible user preference in having a completely network-isolated VC, in which case there would be no BYOB (well, ok, maybe from SSE). In those cases the information would still be relevant for Vero/Vouch to pick one of the responses.
